findings.finding: Any VID can be a party. Personhood, uniqueness and Sybil resistance are left to an unnamed consumer trust framework
Identity and proof validation are not authorization, and ceremony membership grants nothing
No shared component may default a quorum, but the two-voucher rule must still be set by the community
Vouch meaning isn't defined here; the spec only proves which exchange happened and that it completed
Multi-party onboarding is only linked bilateral tasks; the ceremony vocabulary is out of scope
Nothing requires or prevents in-person vouching. Exclusion would be written into uncovered layers, so no inclusion check exists
Signed, durable role-change records give a forensic trail of how privilege was acquired
Revocation, cascade and consequences for honest vouchers are absent; task control only stops in-flight work
Status is re-checked before each irreversible effect, so a revoked insider's queued actions stop
No due-process path, and tightly bounded errors limit what a refused person learns
A community VID counts as `public` and makes documents joinable; pairwise is only a SHOULD
Outcome evidence discloses whole documents; unlinkability goes to VTI, and ZK isn't referenced
Minimisation is a SHOULD in an informative section; nothing binds a vouching task to withholding nationality, employer or location
No envelope member binds an agent's action to a principal or mandate
Task specs may not declare that human approval is required, so human review of agent work lives only in each consumer's policy
Nothing addresses slow trust accumulation, pressure campaigns or coordinated behaviour; minimised correlators also limit cluster detection
Language tagging and accessibility are deferred, and the dense normative prose is hard to translate. Proposed EX-RK "Normative Text Inaccessible in Translation"
"Portable" means across implementations, not reputation
Security and Privacy Considerations are mostly informative, and there's no conformance suite yet
PHC uniqueness is per issuer and enforced only by governance, so sock puppets can each carry a PHC from a different VTC
A VRC carries no semantics: not how the parties met, strength, scope or expiry; `validUntil` is optional
VRCs need no membership or personhood, so sock puppets can mint a dense VRC web; only a verifier's anchor set filters it
Any VRC counterparty can endorse, with weight left to the community, so endorsement laundering is open
No path to retract a vouch: status exists only for VDC and VAC, the VMC lifecycle is deferred, and a vetter withdraws by telling the community
Role is kept apart from relationship: maintainer rights belong in a time-limited VAC, never inferred from vouches
Nothing detects slow trust accumulation, pressure campaigns or vouch collusion. Proposed EX-RK "Patient-insider trust-to-privilege conversion"
After discovery only the VAC tree cascades. The insider's VRCs, VECs, VWCs and VICs stay verifiable, and there is no "issuer disqualified" signal
No due process (reasons, notice, appeal) for revocation or exclusion
ZK minimum disclosure is a requirement, not a construction; holders present whole credentials today
DTG schemas carry no nationality, but the spec's own community example discloses `issuingCountry`, with no guidance limiting such attributes
Pairwise identifiers plus ZK by default also hide sock-puppet clusters, and this is never discussed. Proposed EX-RK "Privacy-shielded Sybil cluster"
Reputation is deliberately local, which contradicts the white paper's "100% portable"
`taskContext` and its digest are durable correlators, even under ZK
Agent acts are attributable, but nothing marks a subject as an agent rather than a human, and a lent key looks like the person
Revoking a principal's VAC withdraws every agent attenuation beneath it; `any` never includes `modelTraining`
Internationalisation and accessibility are deferred; human-readable values need no language tag
Normative force is unclear: Security Considerations is informative but made binding by Conformance; RFC 8174 is not cited; two items are numbered 8
No in-person requirement, but invitations and "several from distinct vetters" favour the well-connected, with no inclusion guidance
The editor's note calls Trust Tasks outcome evidence "not yet released", but Trust Tasks defines it, so the minimum version is unstated
Admission via 023/024 hides vouchers and vetters, so after discovery the VTC can't learn who vouched for or vetted the insider. There is no escrow or threshold-reveal option
Record 023 checks only the voucher's membership, never the VRC's own revocation, so a retracted vouch still counts. Record 010 does check the VRC
No construction proves a unique person, so Sybil resistance rests entirely on the PHC issuer and the VTC
Self-vouching is not excluded inside the proof: 023 has no clause, and 024's Groth16 route lacks the built clause
Record 024 tokens can be pooled across vetters, and neither cap profile limits the number of distinct people
The privacy that protects members also hides sock-puppet clusters, and no third party can audit admission. The trade-off is never stated
Record 020 hides the principal, with no path to identify them after misuse, and doesn't establish authorisation of the act
An agent holding a person's secret satisfies every clause, so agent and human acts can't be told apart
VRC meaning (whether it's a vouch, how the parties met, competence scope) lies outside the proof
The Linux admission statement (023 or 024) is undecided (WG-16). The two give very different evidence and set very different barriers for Dewi
Event-mode vetting narrows anonymity and, in my assessment, favours conference attendees
The Linux PCS route is an unaudited research artifact and nothing has been reproduced. It isn't post-quantum safe
The revocation delay bound is a MUST in an informative section and is left unset
MUSTs appear in informative sections; records are dense and English-only, with no language tags
Revocation cascade covers only authority chains. Nothing re-examines members a discovered insider vouched for
Portability is holder-chosen linkage proving only existence and non-revocation. Reputation is absent
An admission proof can be counted twice unless the community mints a per-applicant challenge, and that is only a "should"
Editorial: record 013 is called "still requested" but is at `specified`

local_risks.description: Vouch accountability loss under hidden admission: privacy-preserving admission leaves no way to learn who vouched for or vetted a member after an incident.
Patient-insider trust-to-privilege conversion: genuine relationships built over years are converted into privileged roles, then abused.
Privacy-shielded Sybil cluster: pairwise identifiers and ZK presentation hide coordinated sock-puppet clusters from the community.
Normative text inaccessible in translation: dense or ambiguous normative language is misread by implementers using machine translation.

themes.title: Who stops sock puppets?
themes.question: Personhood and uniqueness
themes.summary: All three specs defer personhood and uniqueness: Trust Tasks to an unnamed consumer trust framework, Credentials to each PHC issuer's governance (uniqueness only "in the scope of the PHC issuer"), ZKP to issuers ("personhood is never inferred"). Sock puppets with PHCs from different or lax communities pass every check. The Jia Tan defence rests entirely on VTC governance.

themes.title: What does a vouch mean, and can it be taken back?
themes.question: Vouching semantics and retraction
themes.summary: Trust Tasks proves which exchange happened but leaves vouch meaning to Credentials. A Credentials VRC carries only a subject id, and its lifecycle (withdrawal, revocation) is deferred to the planned DTG Core Trust Task Protocols, which don't exist yet. ZKP record 023 counts a vouch without checking the VRC's own revocation. A retracted vouch can still count.
themes.owner_gap: Unpublished DTG Core Trust Task Protocols

themes.title: Knowing someone is not the same as holding maintainer rights
themes.question: Role versus relationship
themes.summary: All three specs separate who a person is, and who knows them, from what they may do. Trust Tasks: validation "MUST NOT, by itself" be authorization; Credentials: a VAC, not vouches, confers authority, and must expire; ZKP: authority and membership stay separate credentials. This blocks the "enough vouches = maintainer" shortcut, if the kernel community actually uses it.

themes.title: After discovery: who vouched for Kestrel, and what happens to his vouches?
themes.question: Revocation, cascade, forensics, due process
themes.verdict: Missing, and privacy makes it harder
themes.summary: Only authority (VAC) revocation cascades. The vouches, endorsements and invitations Kestrel issued stay verifiable; there is no "issuer disqualified" signal. Under hidden-voucher admission (ZKP 023/024) the community can't learn who vouched for or vetted him. No spec offers due process for anyone wrongly accused. Trust Tasks does stop his queued actions.
themes.owner_gap: Between Credentials, Trust Tasks and governance

themes.title: Privacy that protects Dewi also hides sock-puppet clusters
themes.question: Privacy versus Sybil detection
themes.summary: Pairwise identifiers, fresh correlators and ZK presentation protect Dewi from being tracked across projects. The same features hide coordinated clusters and stop third parties auditing admission. None of the three specs names the trade-off or says who decides the balance.

themes.title: Can Dewi get in from Jakarta?
themes.question: Entry without in-person access
themes.verdict: Not blocked by the specs; exclusion would be built in governance
themes.summary: No spec requires in-person meeting; video, prior acquaintance and even paper transport are allowed. But who may invite, how many vouchers, and which method counts are all community governance, with no inclusion guidance. ZKP 023 needs two member VRCs (a network-position barrier); 024 does not, and Linux has not chosen between them. Event-mode vetting favours conference-goers.

themes.title: Whose agent wrote this patch?
themes.question: AI agent contributions
themes.verdict: Partly; accountability after misuse is missing
themes.summary: Credentials has the best model: an agent acting under a VAC acts as itself with a traceable chain, and revocation cascades to agents. But nothing marks a subject as an agent rather than a human; a lent key looks like the person; ZKP 020 deliberately hides the principal with no route back after misuse; and Trust Tasks bars specs from requiring human approval.
themes.owner_gap: Between Credentials, Trust Tasks and ZKP

themes.title: "100% portable" reputation
themes.question: Portability
themes.summary: The white paper promises a personal trust graph that is "100% portable" across projects. In the specs, reputation is deliberately local: each verifier configures what it accepts, vetting is scoped to one community, and carrying reputation means choosing to be linkable. Coherent and privacy-protective, but not what the case study claims.

themes.title: Can Dewi tell what MUST means?
themes.question: Language, accessibility, normative clarity
themes.verdict: Deferred in all three, with contradictions
themes.summary: Language tagging, internationalisation and accessibility are deferred in all three. Two specs put binding MUSTs in sections marked informative. Dense normative prose is hard to machine-translate. For an implementer reading in translation, it is unclear which requirements bind.

themes.title: The specs out of step with each other
themes.question: Cross-spec version and reference skew
themes.summary: Credentials says Trust Tasks outcome evidence is "not yet released", but Trust Tasks defines it. Trust Tasks never references the ZKP spec. ZKP's own reading guide is out of date. Each relies on the others for parts of the scenario, without pinning versions.

meta.scenario: SC-LX: Linux kernel maintainers as a Verifiable Trust Community
meta.source: First Person Project White Paper V2.0, Part Eight
meta.method: One AI subagent per spec, read-only, citing path:line; main session spot-checked 27 cited lines; all matched. Findings are AI-drafted and await Nicky's review.
